title: Honda V6 (2008-2012 Accord V6, 2008-2010 Odyssey EX-L/Touring, 2009-2013 Pilot): fouled plugs and misfires P0301-P0304 from piston rings (bulletins 13-078, 13-080, 13-082)
summary: On these Honda V6s, the piston rings on certain cylinders can rotate and line up, letting oil foul the spark plugs and setting misfire codes P0301-P0304 on cylinders 1-4. Honda's fix comes in two stages: first a PCM software update and new plugs (Procedure A); if it comes back, clean the pistons and replace the rings plus plugs (Procedure B). Under the Soto class settlement, Honda covered this repair for 8 years with unlimited mileage from the original purchase date.
warnings: Honda requires Procedure A (software and plugs) and the car returned to the owner before any piston ring work, unless the software is already current.

specs.name: Warranty extension (Soto settlement)
specs.value: 8 years, unlimited mileage, from the original purchase date, for misfire repairs that set P0301-P0304
specs.note: Counted from purchase, so 2008-2013 vehicles have aged out. Not available on total-loss, salvage or branded-title vehicles.

specs.name: Labor, Procedure B on Odyssey (rings 1-3, plugs 1-4)
specs.value: 8.5 h, plus 0.8 h if cylinder 4 rings are also done

steps.text: Check for P0301, P0302, P0303 or P0304. None stored: the bulletin doesn't apply.
Pull the spark plug on each cylinder with a misfire code. If the plugs aren't fouled, the bulletin doesn't apply.
Compare the PCM software ID with Honda's minimum. If it's older, Procedure A: update the PCM, replace all four plugs on cylinders 1-4, and return the car to the owner.

If it returns with fouled plugs after Procedure A (or the software was already current), Procedure B: clean the pistons and replace the rings on cylinders 1-3, or 1-4 if P0304 is stored, plus replace plugs 1-4. Honda's procedure does this without removing the engine or crankshaft.

body: Honda's bulletins tell owners to check with a dealer, since the procedures are for trained technicians with the right tools.
